clue.text: Affliction may be bland

parts.note: the word be sounds like the letter B, which it stands for here
light food or entertainment is mild and unchallenging, so bland

explanation.surface: Someone shrugs that a hardship can sometimes be dull and uneventful.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'bland' as B-LAND, then swap LAND for its opposite-feeling partner: 'be' gives B and 'bland' gives LIGHT, a trick typical of this setter.
explanation.definitionFit: A blight is a plague or curse that spoils things, so an affliction in both literal and figurative senses.

clue.text: Primitive draw?

parts.note: the second half of the answer

explanation.surface: A crude, early sort of sketch, as cave art might be.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: the answer read as an instruction, WARD written back, produces the clue's single word 'draw'.
explanation.definitionFit: Backward describes something undeveloped or behind the times, which is what primitive means.

clue.text: Like some units taking a risk

indicators.note: taking here means taking away, so the letter is removed

parts.note: imperial units are the old British measures such as pints, feet and pounds

explanation.surface: Army units seem to be doing something dangerous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking' looks like 'carrying' but means removing: A comes out of IMPERIAL.
explanation.definitionFit: To imperil something is to put it in danger, which is to risk it as a verb.

clue.text: Delinquent hangout in which one toilet is turned upside down

indicators.note: in which says the next pieces go inside the jumbled hang

parts.note: split as HANG plus OUT: out tells you to jumble the letters of hang

indicators.note: in a down entry, turning upside down reads the letters from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I
loo is the everyday British word for a toilet

explanation.surface: A youth's den where a lavatory has been upended by vandals.
explanation.walkthrough: The trick is splitting 'hangout': its last three letters are the anagram signal for the first four. In a down entry 'turned upside down' means read from the bottom, a reversal.
explanation.definitionFit: A hooligan is a young troublemaker or lout, a delinquent in the noun sense.

clue.text: Arrogant, if true

definitions.meaning: presumptuous, taking too much upon oneself
a conjunction meaning supposing that, on the premise that

explanation.surface: Someone haughty, provided the report is accurate.
explanation.definitionFit: Assuming means both presumptuous in manner and, as a conjunction, provided that something holds.

clue.text: Under shelf is another essay on a time when there's little to report

definitions.text: a time when there's little to report

indicators.note: in a down entry, putting one piece under another means it follows it

parts.note: a sill is the ledge or shelf at the foot of a window

indicators.note: another version of the words essay on means their letters remade in a new order

explanation.surface: A student writes yet another essay, kept beneath the shelf, during a quiet spell.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'Under' places the second piece below the first; 'another' is an unusual anagram signal, a different version of the words.
explanation.definitionFit: The silly season is the summer lull when newspapers, short of real news, print trivial stories.

clue.text: Seizes unfinished extortion note

indicators.note: unfinished means the last letter is cut off the word

parts.note: usury is lending money at an extortionate rate of interest
PS, a postscript, is a note added at the end of a letter

explanation.surface: Grabbing an incomplete ransom note from a blackmailer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfinished' drops the Y of USURY to leave USUR.
explanation.definitionFit: To usurp is to take power or a position by force, so it is to seize as a verb.

clue.text: Philistine drinks too much of this element

parts.note: Philistine is the setter, who refers to themself as I
so, as in 'I'm so tired', means to an excessive degree
to tope is to drink alcohol heavily

explanation.surface: The setter confesses to over-indulging in this element, perhaps a spirit.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter's pseudonym stands for I. Read 'drinks too much' as I SO TOPE: I drink so much.
explanation.definitionFit: An isotope is one form of a chemical element, differing in neutron number; strictly 'of this element' covers it.

clue.text: Table container would make easy money, if switched to rail

indicators.note: the transport in the answer is swapped for another kind

parts.note: a gravy train is a source of money for little effort
a train is the means of transport that runs on rail

explanation.surface: A tableware item would earn a fortune if it ran on rails.
explanation.walkthrough: Change the boat in the answer for the transport that runs on rail, a train, and you get a gravy train, easy money.
explanation.definitionFit: A gravy boat is the jug in which sauce is served at the dining table.

clue.text: Jailer to break up our act? Not us!

indicators.note: to break the words up our act is to smash their letters into a new order
not here means leaving the next letters out of the mix

parts.note: us read as U's, the plural of the letter U

explanation.surface: A prison officer intervening in a double act, insisting it is not theirs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to break' rearranges UPOURACT, and 'Not us' removes the two U's (read 'us' as U's), leaving the letters of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A captor is one who holds another prisoner, so close to a jailer, though the fit is loose.

clue.text: Most glad with you finally getting some kind of sleep in this medical condition

indicators.note: most of a word means all but its last letter
finally picks the last letter of the word

parts.note: a coma is a deep unconscious state, a kind of sleep

explanation.surface: A patient is happiest when, at last, an odd sort of slumber comes with their eye disease.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Most' trims GLAD to GLA; 'finally' takes U from 'you'.
explanation.definitionFit: Glaucoma is an eye disease in which raised pressure damages the optic nerve.

clue.text: Beethoven's third, fifth, sixth and ninth: my copy is ear-shattering

indicators.note: shattering breaks the letters apart into a new order

parts.note: the fifth, sixth and ninth letters of the composer's name are H, O and N

explanation.surface: A listener complains that their recording of several Beethoven symphonies is deafening.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beethoven's third' is the definition, but the clue reuses the name: its fifth, sixth and ninth letters join MY COPY IS EAR before 'shattering' rearranges them all.
explanation.definitionFit: Beethoven's Symphony No. 3 in E flat is nicknamed the Eroica, Italian for heroic.

clue.text: Fans of a heartless romance, drink up

indicators.note: heartless removes the central letter

parts.note: a romance is a novel, a work of fiction

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the word reads from bottom to top

parts.note: soda is a fizzy drink

explanation.surface: Followers of a cold-hearted love story are told to finish their drinks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' drops the T at the centre of FICTION; 'up' turns SODA to ADOS.
explanation.definitionFit: Aficionados are keen followers or enthusiasts of a pursuit, so fans.

clue.text: Fractured ankle is bad, in pieces

indicators.note: letters in pieces have been broken apart and reassembled differently

explanation.surface: A broken ankle is a nasty injury, all in bits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fractured' looks like the anagram signal, but it is the definition; 'in pieces' does the rearranging.
explanation.definitionFit: Balkanised means split into small, often hostile units, like the states of the Balkans, so fractured.

clue.text: Once more committed a boring and endless reformation

indicators.note: a reformation re-forms the letters into a new arrangement
endless cuts off the final letter

explanation.surface: A newly devout convert who has turned a dull life around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' trims AND to AN; 'reformation' rearranges A, BORING and AN.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone born-again has experienced a renewed religious conversion, recommitting to faith.

clue.text: Note: get up and learn

parts.note: a memo is a short written note
to rise is to get up out of bed

explanation.surface: A reminder to wake up and study.
explanation.definitionFit: To memorise is to commit something to memory, a way of learning it by heart.

clue.text: Hiding poor result by blowing

indicators.note: the word by hides the other letters inside itself
poor signals the letters are in a bad order and need sorting

explanation.surface: Someone covers up a bad outcome with lots of bluster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hiding' reads like a thrashing, but it is the containment signal, with an implied comma after 'result'; 'poor' shuffles the word it follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Blustery weather is gusty and windy, so a day that is blowing hard.

clue.text: See 14
Google site reporting enhanced cleavage?

indicators.note: reporting means the words are as heard spoken

parts.note: a cleavage enlarged by silicone implants could be called a silicone ...

explanation.surface: A web search turns up a site with surgically improved busts.
explanation.walkthrough: The extra E of silicone, the implant gel, is silent when spoken.
explanation.definitionFit: Google is headquartered in the Californian tech hub around Santa Clara, nicknamed for its chip makers.

clue.text: Dawn French in romantic sitcom that starts not too demanding

indicators.note: starts takes the opening letter of each of the five words before it

parts.note: light work or reading is easy and undemanding

explanation.surface: The comedian Dawn French stars in a gentle romcom series.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dawn French' is the English comic actress, but the name splits: 'Dawn' is the definition and 'French' starts the run of initial letters.
explanation.definitionFit: First light is the moment the sky first brightens in the morning, so daybreak.

clue.text: Fag end found by less energetic tradesman

indicators.note: the end of a word is its last letter

parts.note: lazier means more idle, so less energetic

explanation.surface: A cigarette butt left by an idle worker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fag' is British slang for a cigarette, and 'Fag end' a butt; here 'end' picks the G.
explanation.definitionFit: A glazier is a skilled worker who fits glass into windows, a tradesman.

clue.text: See 17
Spilling fine ale a reason for such a biting rebuke

indicators.note: spilling the words lets the letters fall out in a new order

explanation.surface: Knocking over a pint of good beer earns a sharp telling-off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'biting' plays on the flea's bite.
explanation.definitionFit: To send someone off with a flea in their ear is to give them a sharp scolding.

clue.text: See 1
Praise for current company getting a new deal

parts.note: AC is alternating current

indicators.note: a new version of the word deal is a fresh arrangement of its letters

explanation.surface: Applause for a firm that has signed a fresh contract.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a new' rearranges DEAL to LADE; the 'a' is part of the signal, as in 'a new rendering of'.
explanation.definitionFit: An accolade is an award or expression of admiration, so a form of praise.

clue.text: This picks up light wine, if essentially deficient

indicators.note: lacking its essence means the central letter goes

parts.note: retsina is a Greek white wine flavoured with pine resin

explanation.surface: A light wine that lacks something at its core.
explanation.walkthrough: 'light' looks like an adjective for the wine, but belongs to the definition; 'if essentially deficient' drops the middle S of RETSINA.
explanation.definitionFit: The retina is the light-sensitive layer at the back of the eye that detects images.

clue.text: Undue interference shown ultimately by grandmother is my problem

parts.note: nan is an informal British word for a grandmother

indicators.note: ultimately picks the very last letter
a problem with the words is my means their letters are muddled

explanation.surface: A grandparent's meddling is causing me trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ultimately' takes N from 'shown'; 'problem' turns IS MY into YISM.
explanation.definitionFit: Nannyism is excessive, overprotective interference in others' lives, as by a nanny state.

clue.text: Heavy breather ignored, extremely cross

indicators.note: extremely takes the extremes, first and last letters, of each word

explanation.surface: An irate person ignored by a heavy-breathing caller.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cross' looks like 'angry', but is the noun for a mix.
explanation.definitionFit: A hybrid is a mixture of two breeds or kinds, so a cross in the breeding sense.
